steps.say: Retroperitoneal fibrosis, also called Ormond disease, is a slowly growing sheet of inflamed scar tissue behind the abdominal cavity. The plaque sits over the lumbar spine and the front of the aorta, stretching between the fourth lumbar and first sacral vertebrae. As it hardens it traps both ureters, the tubes carrying urine from kidney to bladder, and slowly strangles them shut.
steps.tx: **Retroperitoneal fibrosis** (fibro inflammatory scar sheet behind the belly cavity, also called **Ormond disease**) forms a plaque centred over the **lumbar spine** (lower back bones) and anterior aorta between **L4 and S1** (fourth lumbar to first sacral vertebrae). The hardening mantle **entraps the ureters** (urine tubes from kidney to bladder) on both sides, so progressive extrinsic compression ends in bilateral obstruction unless the plaque is recognised and treated.

rows: Lumbar spine and anterior aorta, L4-S1 span

steps.say: Most cases have no obvious cause, and up to 70 percent of these idiopathic cases belong to one modern family of disorders. They are part of systemic IgG4 related disease, in which the blood carries raised IgG4 antibodies and the tissue fills with dense IgG4 positive plasma cells and lymphocytes. Finding raised serum IgG4 points to a steroid responsive illness rather than a cancer, which changes the whole plan.
steps.tx: Up to **50% to 70%** (five to seven in ten) of idiopathic cases belong to systemic **IgG4-related disease** (antibody driven multi organ fibro inflammation), with elevated **serum IgG4** (raised blood antibody level) and dense **IgG4-positive lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates** (plasma cell and lymphocyte invasion of tissue). An IgG4 rich biopsy therefore predicts **steroid responsiveness** (shrinkage with corticosteroids) and steers the patient away from cancer surgery toward medical therapy.

steps.say: The classic imaging triad is taught on intravenous or CT urography and never changes. First the middle thirds of both ureters are pulled toward the midline, second they narrow from outside pressure at the L4 L5 level, and third the kidneys above swell with trapped urine. Medial deviation plus smooth extrinsic narrowing plus upstream hydroureteronephrosis is retroperitoneal fibrosis until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Read the classical triad on **intravenous or CT urography** (contrast imaging of the urinary tract): **medial deviation** (midline pull) of the middle ureters, **extrinsic ureteral narrowing** (outside pressure stricture) at **L4-L5** (fourth to fifth lumbar level, classic L4-L5 narrowing), and proximal **hydroureteronephrosis** (swollen kidney and ureter above the block). This three part picture is so characteristic that its presence makes retroperitoneal fibrosis the working diagnosis while malignancy is being excluded.

vis.caption: Hydronephrosis on intravenous urogram: upstream swelling above the fibrotic narrowing. Credit: Cambridge University Press.

steps.say: A malignant lookalike demands respect, because lymphoma, sarcoma, and metastatic carcinoma can all seed the retroperitoneum. The malignant plaque behaves in the opposite way: it pushes the ureters outward to the sides instead of pulling them inward, and it climbs above the kidney vessels up to the L2 level. Lateral deviation with high cephalad spread means biopsy first, because steroids alone would waste precious time.
steps.tx: Suspect **malignant retroperitoneal fibrosis** (malignant RPF: lymphoma, sarcoma, or metastatic carcinoma seeding the back cavity) when the plaque **displaces the ureters laterally** (pushes tubes outward to the sides) and **expands cephalad above the renal vessels** (climbs toward the head past the kidney arteries at **L2**, second lumbar level). Benign disease pulls ureters medially and stops low, while malignant spread pushes them laterally and climbs high, so atypical imaging earns a deep biopsy before any steroids.

steps.say: Active non malignant disease is treated with medicines first, and corticosteroids lead the attack. Prednisolone starts near one milligram per kilogram per day for four weeks, then tapers slowly over six to nine months while pain, kidney function, and plaque thickness are watched. Tamoxifen or mycophenolate join as steroid sparing partners when steroids alone cannot hold the disease or their side effects bite.
steps.tx: Start active non-malignant disease on systemic **corticosteroids** (anti inflammatory steroids): **prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day** (one milligram per kilogram daily) for **4 weeks** (four weeks), tapered over **6 to 9 months** (six to nine months), with or without **tamoxifen** (selective oestrogen modulator) or **mycophenolate** (antiproliferative immunosuppressant). Track pain, creatinine, and plaque thickness through the taper, and add the steroid sparing partner early when steroids alone fail or toxicity mounts.

steps.say: Surgery is reserved for ureters that stay trapped despite medicines, or where cancer was once on the table. Ureterolysis means carefully peeling each ureter free from the fibrotic mantle along its whole buried length. The freed ureter must not be dropped back into the same scar, so it is transposed sideways into the peritoneal cavity, called intraperitonealization, or wrapped in a tongue of omentum that feeds it blood and keeps scar away.
steps.tx: Perform **surgical ureterolysis** (freeing trapped ureters from scar) by liberating each entrapped ureter from the **fibrotic mantle** (hard scar casing) along its buried course. Then prevent re-entrapment with lateral transposition into the peritoneal cavity, called **intraperitonealization** (nesting the ureter inside the belly lining), or with **omental wrapping** (covering the ureter in fatty apron tissue). Wide retroperitoneal exposure, as in pelvic vascular surgery, gives the safe plane for this dissection.

steps.say: Always ask about medicines, because several everyday drugs can trigger secondary fibrosis. Methysergide and ergotamine, the old migraine remedies, are the classic culprits, and beta blockers plus hydralazine, both blood pressure drugs, are well documented causes too. Stopping the offending drug is part of treatment, and the drug history must be recorded before the plaque is labelled idiopathic.
steps.tx: Review medicines before calling disease idiopathic, because **methysergide** (old migraine drug), **ergotamine** (ergot migraine remedy), **beta-blockers** (blood pressure slowing drugs), and **hydralazine** (direct vessel relaxing drug) are documented culprits in **secondary drug-induced retroperitoneal fibrosis** (scar disease triggered by medicines). Withdraw the offending agent as part of therapy, and record a full drug history in every new plaque, since rechallenge can reawaken the fibrosis.

steps.say: Steroid courses run for many months, so the response needs an objective meter rather than guesswork. The 18F FDG PET CT scan lights up metabolically active inflammation inside the plaque, and the glow fades as corticosteroids and immunosuppressants take hold. Rising uptake warns of relapse during the taper, while a cold quiet plaque supports stepping treatment down safely.
steps.tx: Monitor therapy with **18F-FDG PET-CT scan** (glucose tracer imaging of inflammation), which measures **inflammatory metabolic activity** (sugar hunger of active immune cells) within the retroperitoneal plaque. Bright uptake marks active disease needing full treatment, and fading uptake tracks **therapeutic response** (plaque cooling under drugs) to **corticosteroids and immunosuppressants** (steroids plus immune dampening medicines). Rebrightening during taper warns of relapse before creatinine climbs.
